requirement: Navigation alignment is complete before data logging begins
source: MX60 QSG Rev B, §5.3 p.11 — "Navigation alignment must be done first before data logging is allowed!"
enforced: Software — TMI does not allow logging until alignment is done

requirement: A mission is at least 30 minutes long
source: MX60 QSG Rev B, §5.4 p.13 — "Important! A minimum mission time of >=30 min is required." Repeated §6 p.14
qualification: Trimble states the requirement but not whether TMI enforces it, and gives no reason. V-18

requirement: A ground control point and its picked target are no more than 30 m (100 ft) apart
source: TBC 22905 — "NOTE: The distance in a pair of points cannot exceed the allowed maximum distance of 30 meters (or 100 feet)."
enforced: Software — stated as an allowed maximum that cannot be exceeded
qualification: The topic states the limit. It does not describe what TBC does when a pair exceeds it

requirement: At least one control point in a registration is not a validation point
source: TBC 22905 — "If you set all the selected ground control points (GCPs) as validation points (VPs), an error will pop-up and will prompt you to have at least one ground control point (GCP) for the calculation."
enforced: Software — an error blocks the calculation

requirement: Data outside the outermost control point is not described as registered to that control
source: TBC 22905 — Local is "suitable for a local adjustment of a run, not for systematic error along the run or for adjusting outside the ground control points set" (W-08)
enforced: None — the software gives no indication of where the adjustment stopped
qualification: Trimble states the scope of the method, not a prohibition. What follows — that unadjusted data is not described as adjusted — is a statement of fact, not a Parametrix policy choice

requirement: A calibration is not accepted on RMS alone; a visual check is performed
source: TBC 24886 — "Good RMS values do not mean that the calibration succeeded. A visual check is needed. On the other side, bad RMS values mean that the calibration failed."

requirement: A registration is not judged on its residuals alone; a visual check is performed
source: TBC 25096 — the same sentence, word for word, in the run-to-run registration topic
qualification: Trimble writes "calibration" in both topics. One of the two is a registration topic, which is why it is read as covering both

requirement: Vehicle speed does not exceed 110 km/h (68 mph), system operating or not
source: MX60 UG Rev B, p.53 specification table — "Maximum Vehicle Speed (with operating or non-operating system on board) 110 km/h (68 mph)"
qualification: The specification table states it as the maximum. The body text at p.9 words it "should not exceed"

requirement: Supply voltage is kept above the Battery Protect thresholds
source: MX60 UG Rev B, p.27 — audible warning below 10.5 V for longer than 12 s; power cut below 10.5 V for more than 90 s; normal status recovered if voltage rises above 12.0 V within those 90 s
enforced: Hardware — the Power Unit cuts power itself (W-11)
qualification: The roughly 78 s of usable warning is arithmetic from the two published figures, not a Trimble number

requirement: The system is operated inside its rated environmental envelope
source: MX60 UG Rev B, p.53 — operating -10 to +50 C, 20-80 % RH, footnote 1: "Not exposed to direct sun and without driving less than 10 km/h (6 mph)"
qualification: The temperature rating is conditional. Stationary or below 10 km/h in direct sun is outside the stated envelope, whatever the air temperature
